description: World's most-used blogging and CMS engine.

promotion.reason: Approved by the owner. The Runtipi definition runs WordPress 7.1.0 with MariaDB pinned to 11.4.13. A September 30 managed-Windows proof installed the site, published an exact unique post and read it after restart and keep-data reinstall; all owned resources were removed. Reviewed storage pins keep both POSIX-sensitive data paths on Docker named volumes.

data_storage: Docker named volumes for WordPress files and MariaDB; generated database credentials remain in the managed app folder
risk_notes: Creates 2 Docker containers and publishes one port on this computer's loopback interface only.
Generates 2 credentials of its own, keeps them beside the app's data, and reuses them if you reinstall.
Keeps WordPress files and MariaDB in Docker named volumes and generated database credentials in the managed app folder. A keep-data uninstall retains them; deleting data removes them.
Proven on Windows with Docker's Linux engine. macOS and Linux hosts are unverified.

Opens to WordPress's own installer, which asks you to name the site and create the administrator account. Themes and plugins you add later are code that runs on your computer, so install them from sources you trust.

storage_pins.reason: WordPress writes application files and updates their ownership, which a Windows-backed WSL bind mount cannot reliably support.
MariaDB initialization needs POSIX ownership and permissions, which a Windows-backed WSL bind mount cannot provide.

image_pins.reason: The Runtipi definition runs its database on MariaDB 11.1.3, built 2024-02-09. 11.1 was a short-term release and reached end of life in August 2024, so it has had no security fixes for two years. 11.4 is MariaDB's current long-term release, supported until 2029, and 11.4.13 is its latest patch. WordPress supports any MariaDB from 10.6, a fresh install has no data to migrate, and the audit below covers 11.4.13 because that is what runs.
